newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Spectrum says gets FCC satellite approval.
newsitem.headline: Spectrum says gets FCC satellite approval.

text.p: Spectrum Network Systems Ltd said on Tuesday it had received approval from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) for licensing rights of the Ellipso mobile satellite phone service in parts of Asia Pacific region.
Spectrum said it has the rights for Ellipso in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea as well as Indonesia.

"Ellipso represents a fundamental breakthrough in Spectrum's development of a major presence in telecommunications - not only in Australia but in the expanding and developing Asia Pacific region," managing director Bob Hansford said in a statement.
"Plans for the development and deployment of Ellipso's satellites are well-advanced and construction of satellites will commence later this year," Hansford said.

Spectrum said Ellipso is a global telecommunications system designed to extend and complement existing telephone and data networks. It offers a broad range of modern, satellite-based voice and data communications services.

It said that unlike terrestrial wireless services, Ellipso offered a complete nationwide service to each country it serves, thereby providing service to users located anywhere within national boundaries, no matter how isolated or remote.
Spectrum said Ellipso uses a constellation of medium earth orbiting satellites to connect the user directly to gateways within the existing regional telecommunications networks.
At 12.45 p.m. (0245 GMT), Spectrum shares were 19 cents firmer at 51 cents.
